title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York

direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is very New York-esque, building a jazzy New York world through a lot of shots, zooms, and montages of the city, its buildings, its people, and its skyline, while also building the world of a slightly comedic mystery heist movie; the direction on a microscale centers on John Turturro as part of the old guard, talking with others from his generation who feel the same way about how much the city is changing, while also showing how the new guard and younger generation aren't of his generation, and while the comedic moments are pretty good and the emotional moments are really good, the intense, angry yelling scenes fall flat, as the dialogue isn't written well for them and the actors, even John Turturro, don't hit the right notes; the storytelling is good, as it's a short, well-paced movie with a pretty simple story that doesn't overcomplicate things and keeps you engaged and interested in the main character, his relationships, and his feelings about New York; the tension works well because you become attached to the main character, so you're on your feet when bad things happen to him and when he's trying to pickpocket as a petty crook

performance.comments: Really shows his charisma and experience in this role as he is able to steal every scene he is in with his experience and comedy; has good chemistry with the cast, especially with him relating to the old guard over how New York has changed; he shows his emotions well, especially in the emotional moments with his daughter and wife, but he is not able to be intense; his performance is so good that you really do care for his struggles and empathize with him, as he isn't a monster despite being a petty criminal
Basically plays every character I have seen him play, but does well in the role and has good chemistry with Turturro in playing a foil in the old guard of New York
Honestly pretty annoying and does not click with the rest of the cast as he feels inexperienced and forced; does not hit the intense notes at all
Really only has one scene, but has pretty good chemistry with Turturro, although the intense notes are not hit that well

Really enjoyed his dynamic with Turturro, as they both represent the old guard of New York that is getting left behind by technology; he is a comedic relief character and shows why he has had such a long career in Hollywood

cast.comments: Works well in supporting Turturro as all the performances flow through him, and he works well in supporting them

story.comments: The concept is your typical 'old guy in New York' story, following an old thief who is past his prime as the city changes too much and technology takes over, almost like the final monologue from No Country for Old Men where the world has passed him by and there's nothing he can do about it, as he gets mixed in with the wrong crowd and has to undo the wrong he caused by pickpocketing; the plot structure is good, as it's only 88 minutes and linear, and I very much enjoyed that they don't overcomplicate it; character writing is good, as John Turturro's character is well written as a pickpocket from an older generation who feels New York and technology have passed him by to the point where he's counting the days and each day matters, while the kid is your typical rich, snobby, arrogant kid, the other old guards share the same sentiments about how the world has changed and how they used to have it good, and the estranged daughter is pretty standard, about what you'd expect

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is your typical old, jazzy, fast-paced New York comedy dialogue, and while it's not the best-written dialogue and falls bland and flat in the intense moments, the emotional moments are written decently well, giving the actors material good enough to play with and making the movie enjoyable, fun, and entertaining; the humor is a big and important aspect of the movie, selling the story, keeping you entertained, and building the personalities and relationships of these old characters; the symbolism centers on a new New York that the old guard can't keep up with, very much like the ending monologue from No Country for Old Men about how the world has changed and gotten evil with nothing they can do about it, while also showing that even though he's a thief, he's an ethical person who only takes what he needs to get by, like when he puts stolen wallets in the mailbox so they get returned, along with how far gone you can be when it comes to salvaging past relationships; the foreshadowing is good enough for such a simple story, tying the movie together well and making the ending feel worth it

score.comments: Fits the tone well as it is very jazzy and aids in the montage sequences and showing the old-guard perspective of New York

soundtrack.comments: Filled with many jazzy tracks to set the tone of an 'old guy in New York' movie

cinematography.comments: Filled with many montage sequences of New York to make it feel like many low-budget films shot in New York that build that world; the rest of the movie is pretty standard in how it's shot

editing.comments: Complements the cinematography well in showing New York through its montage sequences, and does a pretty good job stitching the movie together

sound.comments: Pretty standard for an indie heist thriller

production_design.comments: Effectively uses New York as a setting to make it feel like an evolving character, something that has moved past the old guard

review.pacing: Paced very well, as it's a short 88-minute movie with a simple, linear story that doesn't overcomplicate things
review.climax: Ties the movie together well, as the foreshadowing pays off and makes the ending feel worth it
review.tone: A jazzy, slightly comedic 'old guy in New York' heist movie about an old thief who feels the city has passed him by
review.final_notes: Saw at an AMC Screen Unseen screening on October 19th; this movie feels like a lesser version of Tuner
review.overall: Overall, 'The Only Living Pickpocket in New York' is a well-made and enjoyable 'old guy in New York' movie, carried by John Turturro's charisma and comedy in a jazzy, simple heist story about an old thief who gets mixed in with the wrong crowd as the city passes him by; while the intense moments fall flat, it's a fun, entertaining watch
